For a triangle, \(A+B+C=180^\circ\), so

\[
\sin C=\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B.
\]

Given

\[
\sin A=\frac35,\qquad \sin B=\frac{24}{25},
\]

we have

\[
\cos A=\pm \frac45,\qquad \cos B=\pm \frac7{25}.
\]

Since \(A+B<180^\circ\), \(A\) and \(B\) cannot both be obtuse.

### Case 1: \(A,B\) both acute
\[
\cos A=\frac45,\qquad \cos B=\frac7{25}
\]
\[
\sin C=\frac35\cdot \frac7{25}+\frac45\cdot \frac{24}{25}
=\frac{21}{125}+\frac{96}{125}=\frac{117}{125}.
\]

### Case 2: \(A\) obtuse, \(B\) acute
\[
\cos A=-\frac45,\qquad \cos B=\frac7{25}
\]
\[
\sin C=\frac35\cdot \frac7{25}-\frac45\cdot \frac{24}{25}
=\frac{21-96}{125}=-\frac{75}{125}=-\frac35,
\]
which is impossible since \(C\) is an angle of a triangle.

### Case 3: \(A\) acute, \(B\) obtuse
\[
\cos A=\frac45,\qquad \cos B=-\frac7{25}
\]
\[
\sin C=\frac35\cdot\left(-\frac7{25}\right)+\frac45\cdot \frac{24}{25}
=\frac{-21+96}{125}=\frac{75}{125}=\frac35.
\]

Thus the possible values are

\[
\boxed{\frac{117}{125},\frac35}
\]

The answer is \(\frac{117}{125},\frac35\).
